items.heading: A Cse Degree Leads
items.text: A CSE degree leads to the same broad computer science career tracks as any other computing degree. What it specifically adds is step eligibility and PSU technical-recruitment access, two routes genuinely closed or harder to reach from a BSc or BCA background. Everything else, the actual private-sector job market, competes on demonstrated skill far more than on the degree label.

items.heading: Step (Graduate Aptitude Test
items.text: step (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is open to engineering-degree holders and is the direct step into IIT/IISc M.Tech admissions and most PSU technical recruitment. A BSc or BCA graduate does not qualify for step the same way.

items.heading: Step (Graduate Aptitude Test
items.text: step (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is the single biggest concrete advantage a CSE degree holds over a BSc or BCA. Clearing it opens IIT/IISc and other top-tier M.Tech admissions, and a strong score is also the entry route into a meaningful share of PSU technical recruitment. This is worth preparing for even for a student mainly planning a private-sector career, since it is one exam layered on top of regular coursework, not a separate multi-year commitment, and it keeps both doors open at relatively low cost.

rows: Public-sector undertakings hiring for engineer-designated technical posts commonly require a recognised engineering degree by name, closing that specific door to non-engineering computing graduates regardless of skill.
Roles that sit at the boundary of software and hardware/embedded systems sometimes prefer or require an engineering degree specifically, even when the day-to-day work is heavily software-based.
